candidates.change_summary: Remove the assignment to acc.unlockTime so that the unlock time remains unchanged after a Put call.
Remove the balance update so that msg.value is accepted but acc.balance does not increase.
Remove the modifier's reentrancy lock check so that Put can be executed reentrantly, potentially allowing multiple balance updates in a single transaction.
Always revert by changing require to assert(false) so that Put never succeeds.
Change unlock time assignment to always use block.timestamp, ignoring the argument, so that the recorded unlock time differs.

Replace `{ (bool _s, bytes memory _d) = msg.sender.call{value: _am}(""); _d; if (_s) { acc.balance = sub_uint256(acc.balance, _am); LogFile.AddMessage(msg.sender,_am,"Collect"); } }` with `{ (bool _s, bytes memory _d) = msg.sender.call{value: _am}(""); _d; }` so balance is never deducted.
Replace `acc.balance = sub_uint256(acc.balance, _am);` with `acc.balance = sub_uint256(acc.balance, 0);` so balance is never reduced.
Replace `if( acc.balance>=MinSum && acc.balance>=_am && block.timestamp>acc.unlockTime)` with `if( acc.balance>=MinSum && acc.balance>=_am)` to remove the time lock check.
Replace `acc.balance = sub_uint256(acc.balance, _am);` with `acc.balance = add_uint256(acc.balance, _am);` so balance increases on collect.
Remove the `nonReentrant_` modifier from `Collect` to allow re-entrant calls that may change balance observed later.
Delete `locked_ = true;` from the modifier so re-entrancy guard is ineffective, allowing re-entrant collect that changes balance.
Delete `locked_ = false;` from the modifier so guard stays locked after first call, preventing further collects but initially collect still works.
